bugs.title: Configuration system is inert — settings.json is never read (every documented knob is ignored)
bugs.description: The entire configuration surface (spec/09, README §3) is non-functional. `setConfig()` is dead code — it is never called anywhere in src/. `getConfig()` always returns `validateConfig(undefined)`, i.e. the hard-coded DEFAULT_CONFIG. No code reads `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` or `<cwd>/.pi/settings.json` (grep of src/ for readFile/settings.json/CONFIG_DIR returns zero hits). Pi's ExtensionAPI exposes no getSettings() accessor and no event carries the merged settings object (verified against dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts: ExtensionAPI has no settings method; SessionStartEvent has no settings field), so the only way to honor the PRD's 'Mulligan reads settings.mulligan' contract is to read the files from disk (Pi's documented convention, extensions.md §ctx.cwd) — which the extension never does. Consequently the master `enabled` switch, all thresholds, maxDepth, requireMutationWarning, estimateConfidence, and log.file are all permanently fixed at their defaults. The README's 'Disabling' section (`enabled:false` → 'all four tools refuse cleanly with Mulligan: refused — Mulligan is disabled.') is false.
bugs.reproduction: 1) Put `{ "mulligan": { "enabled": false, "log": { "file": "/tmp/probe.log" }, "rewind": { "maxDepth": 1 } } }` in .pi/settings.json. 2) Run `pi -e ./src/index.ts -e ./test/integration/smoke.ts --session-id probe -p "/mulligan_smoke F-rewind-core" -p "Reply with exactly: OK"`. 3) Observe the rewind SUCCEEDS (`Mulligan: rewound last_turn...`) instead of refusing with 'Mulligan is disabled', and /tmp/probe.log is never created. (Empirically confirmed during this audit; settings were restored afterward.)
bugs.expected: Per spec/09 §1 and README §3: `mulligan.enabled=false` must make the whole extension a no-op (context filter passes through; all four tools refuse). `log.file` must cause JSONL logging to that path. `maxDepth`, thresholds, etc. must take effect. Config must be re-read on /reload.
bugs.actual: Every config knob is ignored. `enabled:false` does not disable anything; `log.file` produces no log; tools never refuse on the master switch. The extension always runs with DEFAULT_CONFIG.
bugs.location: src/index.ts (factory never reads settings / never calls setConfig; session_start handler only calls resetRuntime) and src/config.ts (setConfig exported but never invoked; getConfig caches validateConfig(undefined)).
bugs.suggestedFix: At factory load AND on every `session_start` event (event.reason covers 'reload'), read and merge the global settings file and the project-local `.pi/settings.json` (project-local overriding global, gated on ctx.isProjectTrusted() per Pi's trust rules), then call `setConfig(merged.mulligan)`. Use CONFIG_DIR_NAME from the pi package + ctx.cwd to locate the project file and the agent dir for the global file. Add an integration test that sets mulligan.enabled=false and asserts every tool refuses and the filter passes through.

bugs.title: Stacked `last_tool_call_group` rewinds make originally-hidden content reappear in the model's context
bugs.description: The filter resolves each rewind marker's target LIVE against the current message list on every inference (spec D7). `resolveLastToolCallGroup` returns 'the last toolGroup unit excluding the rewind's own toolCallId'. When a second rewind marker exists, the FIRST rewind's 'last toolGroup' re-resolves to the SECOND rewind's own assistant+result group (because that is now the last non-excluded toolGroup), instead of the span the agent originally shed. Net effect: content the agent explicitly rewound (e.g. a bloated `read` result) reappears in the model's view once a second rewind is created later in the session. This violates the spec §11 composition example (which claims both original tool groups are hidden and both rewind confirmations survive) and, more seriously, violates the core 'permanent soft-delete' guarantee and success criterion #4 ('Hidden content is never silently lost'). The existing composition test (test/pipeline.test.ts ~line 252) does not catch this because it asserts only on role signatures, not on which messages survive. The smoke harness repeatedly flags this as a SOFT caveat ('hideEntryIds not yet implemented — live last_turn resolution moved the target') but hideEntryIds is not a v1 spec feature, so this is an implementation defect against the spec's stated composition contract.
bugs.reproduction: Synthetic test against the pure filterPipeline (reproduces deterministically): messages = [user, asst(read:cRead), toolResult('BIG-READ-OUTPUT'), asst(mulligan_rewind:cR1), toolResult('rewound'), mulligan:note, asst(grep:cGrep), toolResult('GREP-OUTPUT'), asst(mulligan_rewind:cR2), toolResult('rewound'), mulligan:note]; markers = [rewind seq1 last_tool_call_group excludeToolCallId=cR1, rewind seq2 last_tool_call_group excludeToolCallId=cR2]; cfg protectedRoles default. filterPipeline returns [user, asst(read), toolResult(BIG-READ-OUTPUT), asst(rewind1), toolResult(rewound), note, note] — i.e. BIG-READ-OUTPUT is PRESENT. (Verified during audit; the probe asserted JSON.stringify(out).includes('BIG-READ-OUTPUT') === true.)
bugs.expected: Per spec §11: after two `last_tool_call_group` rewinds, BOTH originally-targeted spans (the read and the grep) remain hidden; only the user message, the rewind confirmations, and the notes survive. Hidden content must never reappear in the model's view (permanent soft-delete).
bugs.actual: The first rewind's target drifts onto the second rewind's own group. The originally-hidden bloated read reappears in context; only the grep and rewind#2's confirmation are hidden. The agent's first rewind is silently voided by the second.
bugs.location: src/transforms.ts — `filterPipeline` (re-partitions and re-resolves each rewind against the reduced array) and `resolveLastToolCallGroup` (relative 'last toolGroup excluding own' has no memory of the originally-targeted span).
bugs.suggestedFix: Pin each rewind's resolved target at creation time (store the target entry ids / a stable message anchor in the marker) and have the filter resolve against the pinned anchor rather than re-resolving 'last toolGroup' live. Alternatively, exclude ALL existing rewind-owned toolCallIds (not just the current marker's own) when resolving, so an earlier rewind cannot retarget onto a later rewind's group. Add a composition test that asserts the originally-hidden span's content is ABSENT from the output after a second rewind (assert on content/ids, not just role signatures).

bugs.title: `checkpoint` rewind can hide the protected latest user message (latest:user not enforced)
bugs.description: spec/08 §8 / spec/06 §8 list `latest:user` as a protected role: 'a rewind that would remove the latest user message ... is refused'. `protectedOk()` only enforces `first:user` (it computes iFirstUser and checks min(remove) > iFirstUser; the `latest:user` selector is read from config but never acted on). For `last_turn`, `latest:user` is protected by construction (the resolver only removes indices AFTER iLastUser). But for `checkpoint` granularity, `resolveCheckpoint` removes every index after the checkpoint target, so if a new user message arrived after the checkpoint was set, that user message is removed — crossing the documented latest:user boundary — and protectedOk does not catch it. The rewind tool's step-5b guard only covers the `last_turn && to_previous_prompt` nuclear case, not checkpoint.
bugs.reproduction: Synthetic test against filterPipeline: messages = [user('u0 original'), user('u1 LATEST ask — should be protected'), assistant('work')]; branchEntries root→leaf with a `label` entry `mulligan:checkpoint:cp` whose targetId is the u0 entry; markers = [{seq:1, granularity:'checkpoint', checkpoint:'cp', excludeToolCallId:'x'}]; cfg protectedRoles = ['first:user','latest:user']. filterPipeline returns messages with roles ['user','assistant'] and `JSON.stringify(out).includes('LATEST ask') === false` — the latest user message was hidden. (Verified during audit.)
bugs.expected: Per spec §8, a checkpoint rewind that would remove the latest user message is refused (no marker applied / the filter skips it). The current ask must survive.
bugs.actual: The latest user message is silently removed by the checkpoint rewind even though `latest:user` is in protectedRoles.
bugs.location: src/transforms.ts — `protectedOk` (only checks first:user) and `resolveCheckpoint`; src/tools/rewind.ts — step-5b protected check only covers last_turn/to_previous_prompt.
bugs.suggestedFix: Extend `protectedOk` (or add a checkpoint-specific guard in the rewind tool) to refuse when the removal set contains the latest user message index (iLatestUser), mirroring the to_previous_prompt refusal. Add a unit test asserting a checkpoint rewind before the latest user message is refused.

bugs.title: Filter and depth guard read ALL branches (getEntries) instead of the current branch
bugs.description: `readMarkers()` (src/filter.ts) and `countRewindMarkers()` / `checkpointExists()` (src/tools/rewind.ts) scan `ctx.sessionManager.getEntries()`, which returns entries from EVERY branch, not just the current branch. After a human uses Pi's native `/tree` to navigate or fork, rewind/shrink markers and checkpoint labels created on abandoned sibling branches leak into the active branch: they are applied by the filter and counted toward maxDepth. This matches the spec §1 pseudocode (which also uses getEntries), so it is a latent design issue rather than a deviation, but it is branch-incorrect and can produce surprising behavior in any session that has been branched.
bugs.reproduction: In a session that has been branched via /tree, create a mulligan:rewind marker on branch A, then navigate to sibling branch B and observe that branch B's context filter still applies branch A's rewind (the targeted span is hidden on B too). Equivalently, countRewindMarkers on B includes A's markers, so maxDepth is reached sooner.
bugs.expected: Markers and checkpoints should be scoped to the current branch (getBranch()), so navigating /tree to a different branch does not carry another branch's rewinds/shrinks/checkpoints with it.
bugs.actual: All markers/labels across all branches are read and applied regardless of which branch is active.
bugs.suggestedFix: Read from `ctx.sessionManager.getBranch()` (leaf→root) instead of `getEntries()`, filtering to entries on the active branch. Update the spec pseudocode reference accordingly.

bugs.title: `mulligan_rewind` reports success even when the marker failed to persist
bugs.description: In rewind.ts, `appendRewindMarker` is fail-open and returns `null` if `pi.appendEntry` throws or `getLeafId()` returns null. The tool does NOT check for null: it proceeds to `leaveNote(...)` and returns the success text 'Mulligan: rewound <granularity>. <K> messages will be hidden... Note left.' The agent is told the rewind succeeded and K messages will be hidden, but no marker was persisted, so the filter will hide nothing. This is a silent correctness failure (the agent believes it shed context it is still carrying). The details.markerId field will be null, but the human-facing text is a success message.
bugs.reproduction: Inject a fake pi whose `appendEntry` throws (or whose sessionManager.getLeafId returns null), call the rewind tool with a valid note, and observe the returned text is the success form ('Mulligan: rewound ...') rather than a refusal, despite no marker being persisted.
bugs.expected: If the marker could not be persisted, the tool should return a failure/refusal text (e.g. 'Mulligan: refused — could not persist rewind marker') so the agent is not misled into thinking the span was hidden.
bugs.actual: The tool returns the success text and leaves a note even though no rewind marker exists to drive the filter.
bugs.location: src/tools/rewind.ts — execute step 7 (no null-check on `markerId` before leaveNote + success return).
bugs.suggestedFix: After `const markerId = appendRewindMarker(...)`, if markerId is null, return a refusal text ('could not persist rewind marker') and do not call leaveNote or report success.

bugs.title: `/reload` does not re-read configuration (README §3 inaccuracy)
bugs.description: README §3 states config is 'loaded lazily on first use, cached for the session, and re-read on `/reload`'. The extension's `session_start` handler (which fires with event.reason === 'reload' on /reload) only calls `resetRuntime(sessionId)`; it never re-reads settings or calls setConfig. Combined with BUG-001 (config is never read at all), this means even a correct future load-time read would not be refreshed by /reload unless session_start is wired to do so. This is a documented behavior that does not exist.
bugs.reproduction: After fixing BUG-001's load-time read, change a value in settings.json, run /reload, and observe the old value is still in effect (getConfig cache not refreshed). Today the bug is masked because no value is ever read.
bugs.expected: Per README §3, `/reload` should re-read settings.mulligan and update the cached config.
bugs.actual: session_start only resets the runtime map; config is never re-read on reload.
bugs.suggestedFix: In the session_start handler, (re)read and merge settings (global + trusted project-local) and call setConfig, in addition to resetRuntime. Gate project-local reads on ctx.isProjectTrusted().

bugs.title: Integration smoke harness leaves core spec/10 §2.1 scenarios without deterministic end-to-end proof
bugs.description: The deterministic smoke suite (npm run smoke) passes 9/9, but the authoritative proofs for several PRD scenarios are marked SOFT/model-driven-only and are never asserted deterministically: F-rewind-core (seed hiding — 'hideEntryIds not yet implemented — live last_turn resolution moved the target'), F-checkpoint (K=0 / seed hiding / consumption — three SOFT caveats), F-shrink-preventive (bloatHit:true is 'unprovable in this harness' because the only big-result test tool is a mulligan_* tool which bloatReminderHandler skips), and F-nudge-drift (hasNudge:true requires a >3000-token model turn). The bloatHit and hasNudge paths therefore have no automated proof that they fire in a real session. Additionally scenarios.md documents F-retrycap and F-abortfraction (E22) which reference unimplemented config knobs (rewind.maxRetriesPerPrompt, rewind.abortContextFraction).
bugs.reproduction: Run `npm run smoke` and read the SOFT/NOTE lines; inspect test/integration/scenarios.md for the 'unprovable in this harness' / 'SOFT' / 'model-driven' annotations on F-shrink-preventive, F-nudge-drift, F-rewind-core, F-checkpoint.
bugs.expected: Per spec/10 §2.1/§3 ('Definition of done': all F-* integration scenarios green against a real pi -p run), each scenario should have a deterministic pass criterion exercising the actual mechanism (bloat reminder fires on a real >threshold non-mulligan tool_result; drift nudge injects on a real >threshold turn; rewind/checkpoint deterministically hide the targeted span).
bugs.actual: Four of the nine scenarios have their headline assertions marked SOFT/model-driven; two of those (bloatHit, hasNudge) are explicitly 'unprovable in this harness'. The deterministic suite proves marker persistence and entry shapes, but not the core hiding/firing behaviors for those scenarios.
bugs.location: test/integration/smoke.ts and test/integration/scenarios.md (F-shrink-preventive, F-nudge-drift, F-rewind-core, F-checkpoint).
bugs.suggestedFix: Register a non-mulligan_* test tool in the smoke helper that returns a >threshold result so bloatHit:true is deterministically provable; add a deterministic two-turn drift-nudge scenario (or a unit-level harness that drives the turn_end→context sequence with a controlled >threshold delta); make seed-hiding deterministic by pinning rewind targets (see BUG-002). Drop or clearly mark F-retrycap/F-abortfraction as out-of-scope since their config knobs are not implemented.

bugs.title: `mulligan_audit` Suggestion line is wrong for non-toolResult top messages
bugs.description: renderAuditReport always emits: `Suggestion: the \`<rows[0].label>\` result is the largest contributor. Consider mulligan_shrink.` It hard-codes the word 'result' and always recommends mulligan_shrink, even when rows[0] is a user message or an assistant message (spec/05 §4's example only shows this line for a toolResult). The describeMessage label for a user message is `user "<snippet>"` and for an assistant is `(thinking + toolCall xN)`, so the suggestion reads awkwardly ('the `user "..."` result is the largest contributor. Consider mulligan_shrink.'). Shrink of a non-toolResult is allowed (spec E19) but the description steering is toolResult-oriented, so the suggestion is misleading when the largest carrier is reasoning or a user paste.
bugs.reproduction: Construct a filtered view whose largest message is an assistant message (e.g. heavy thinking) or a large user paste; call renderAuditReport and observe the Suggestion line still says 'result' and 'mulligan_shrink'.
bugs.expected: The suggestion should either only fire when rows[0] is a toolResult (matching the spec example) or phrase itself generically (e.g. 'largest contributor' without 'result', and suggest rewind for assistant turns / shrink for toolResult/user).
bugs.actual: The Suggestion always names rows[0].label as a 'result' and always recommends mulligan_shrink regardless of the top message's role.
bugs.suggestedFix: Gate the mulligan_shrink suggestion on rows[0].role === 'toolResult'; otherwise emit a role-appropriate suggestion (e.g. suggest mulligan_rewind for a heavy assistant turn) or omit the Suggestion line.

summary: Rigorous end-to-end validation against the PRD: full source audit of all 15 src/ modules, real model-driven pi 0.84.1 runs (verified the core single-rewind mechanism works — a bloated result is hidden on the next inference and the model auto-continues, and mulligan_audit reports an accurate filtered token breakdown), the project's own 9/9 smoke harness, plus targeted synthetic tests against the pure filterPipeline. The single-rewind happy path and the fail-open discipline are solid and the 635-test unit suite is green. However I found 2 critical and 6 lesser issues. CRITICAL #1: the entire configuration surface is inert — settings.json is never read (setConfig is dead code; getConfig always returns DEFAULT_CONFIG), so enabled/thresholds/maxDepth/log.file are all ignored (empirically confirmed: mulligan.enabled=false in .pi/settings.json did not disable anything). CRITICAL #2: stacked last_tool_call_group rewinds mis-target — the second rewind causes the first rewind's hidden span to REAPPEAR in the model's context, violating the spec §11 composition contract and the permanent-soft-delete guarantee / success criterion #4 (the existing composition test misses it because it asserts only role signatures, not content). MAJOR: a checkpoint rewind can delete the protected latest user message because protectedOk only enforces first:user. The remaining issues are minor (getEntries reads all branches not the current branch; rewind reports success even when the marker failed to persist; /reload does not re-read config; smoke harness leaves 4 scenarios' headline assertions SOFT/unprovable) and cosmetic (audit Suggestion line). The bugs cluster in two areas needing attention: (a) config wiring (index.ts never reads settings), and (b) the filter's live relative targeting (D7) which breaks under marker stacking and lacks latest:user enforcement for checkpoint.
recommendations: Wire configuration reading: at factory load and on every session_start (reason includes 'reload'), read+merge the global ~/.pi/agent/settings.json and the trusted project-local <cwd>/.pi/settings.json (project-local overrides global, gated on ctx.isProjectTrusted()), then call setConfig(merged.mulligan). Add an integration test that sets mulligan.enabled=false and asserts all four tools refuse and the filter passes through.

Pin each rewind's resolved target at creation time (store target entry ids / a stable message anchor in the marker) and have the filter resolve against the pinned anchor, so a later rewind cannot retarget an earlier one and originally-hidden content cannot reappear. At minimum, exclude ALL existing rewind-owned toolCallIds when resolving 'last toolGroup', not just the current marker's own. Add a composition test that asserts the originally-hidden span's CONTENT is absent after a second rewind (not just role signatures).
Enforce latest:user in protectedOk (or a checkpoint-specific guard in the rewind tool): refuse when the removal set contains the latest user message index, mirroring the to_previous_prompt refusal.
Scope marker/label reads to ctx.sessionManager.getBranch() instead of getEntries() so /tree navigation does not carry another branch's markers forward.

Null-check appendRewindMarker's return value in rewind.ts and return a refusal text (and skip leaveNote) when the marker could not be persisted, so the agent is not told a rewind succeeded when nothing will be hidden.

Add deterministic (non-model) coverage for the currently-SOFT smoke scenarios: register a non-mulligan_* big-result test tool so bloatHit:true is provable; add a controlled two-turn drift-nudge harness; make last_turn/checkpoint seed-hiding deterministic once targets are pinned. Drop or clearly mark F-retrycap/F-abortfraction as out-of-scope (their config knobs maxRetriesPerPrompt/abortContextFraction are not implemented in v1).
